segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Let's begin. The goal today is to lock the Q1 marketing budget.

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: I've shared the sheet. The ask is 22 lakh for the quarter.

segments.speaker: Sameer Gupta
segments.text: That's up from 16 lakh in Q4, so about forty percent more.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: And revenue is up maybe twelve percent. I can't sign forty.

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: Q1 has the trade fair in January and the new product launch. That's where the jump comes from.

segments.speaker: Nandini Hegde
segments.text: From sales, the launch really needs support. The fair, I'm less sure.

segments.speaker: Sameer Gupta
segments.text: The fair alone is 4.5 lakh, with the stall, travel and printing.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: How many leads did we get from the fair last year?

segments.speaker: Nandini Hegde
segments.text: About ninety. Maybe six turned into customers.

segments.speaker: Sameer Gupta
segments.text: So roughly seventy five thousand rupees per customer from the fair.

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: Okay, those numbers aren't great, I'll admit.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Then we skip the January trade fair stall this year.

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: Fine. We take the fair out.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Without the fair, where does the budget land?

segments.speaker: Sameer Gupta
segments.text: 17.5 lakh. I'd keep a small buffer and call it 18.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: 18 lakh is acceptable. Q1 marketing budget is 18 lakh, final.

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: I can work with 18 if the launch money is protected inside it.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Launch money is protected, you decide the split.

segments.speaker: Nandini Hegde
segments.text: Can I make a pitch? An influencer campaign for the launch, around 5 lakh.

segments.speaker: Sameer Gupta
segments.text: That would blow through the 18 straight away.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Not this quarter. Bring me numbers from a small test first and we'll talk.

segments.speaker: Nandini Hegde
segments.text: Okay, I'll park it.

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: The agency retainer is the other big line. They charge 1.8 lakh a month.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: That's high for what we get. Can you renegotiate?

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: I'll renegotiate the agency retainer by end of the month. Their contract renews in December anyway.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Good. Aim for 1.5 or less.

segments.speaker: Sameer Gupta
segments.text: I'll need to rebuild the budget sheet with the fair removed and the new total.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Sameer, please send me the revised budget sheet by 25 November.

segments.speaker: Sameer Gupta
segments.text: 25 November, okay. I'll split it by month as well.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Also, keep in mind the audit committee meets on 3 December, and they'll ask about marketing spend.

segments.speaker: Sameer Gupta
segments.text: I'll keep that deck separate, it needs different detail.

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: We already paid a deposit to the fair organisers, ten thousand.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Is it refundable?

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: Half of it, if we cancel before December.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Then someone has to tell the event organisers we're cancelling the stall, before December.

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: My team is deep in the launch, so I can't promise it'll be me.

segments.speaker: Nandini Hegde
segments.text: Sales spoke to them last year, but that person has left.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Let's not lose that five thousand because nobody wrote an email. Sort it out between you.

segments.speaker: Sameer Gupta
segments.text: Another point, digital ads. Spend there was flat all of Q4.

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: And the cost per click went down, so we got more for the same money.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Keep it flat in Q1 then. No reason to change what works.

segments.speaker: Nandini Hegde
segments.text: Sales would like printed brochures for the launch, maybe two thousand copies.

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: That fits inside the launch money, I'll include it.

segments.speaker: Sameer Gupta
segments.text: Quick reminder that GST on agency invoices went up on the new contract.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Put it in the sheet then, as a separate line.

segments.speaker: Sameer Gupta
segments.text: Will do.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Anything else before we close?

segments.speaker: Nandini Hegde
segments.text: Nothing more from sales.

segments.speaker: Rahul Dutta
segments.text: All good from marketing.

segments.speaker: Anjali Verma
segments.text: Thank you. Let's close it here.

decisions.fact: The January trade fair stall is dropped this year.
The Q1 marketing budget is fixed at 18 lakh.

action_items.fact: Rahul renegotiates the agency retainer, aiming for 1.5 lakh a month or less.
Sameer sends the revised budget sheet split by month.
The event organisers are told the stall is cancelled, to recover half the deposit; nobody named.

distractors.fact: A 5 lakh influencer campaign was pitched and parked.
3 December is the audit committee meeting, not a budget deadline.
